title: Meaning, Soul and Afterlife
welcome_lead: What is the meaning of life — and what happens after we die?
meta_desc: KS3 Religious Studies adventure on the meaning of life, the soul and the afterlife.
final_note: You can now compare different religious views on the soul and what comes next.

walkthroughs.body_html: Religions answer 'what is life for?' in different ways. Christians, Muslims and Jews often say life is about loving and serving God. Hindus aim to escape the cycle of rebirth. Buddhists seek to end suffering. Atheists may make their own meaning.

Many religions teach we have a soul — a spiritual part of us that goes beyond the body. In Christianity, Islam and Judaism the soul lives on after death. In Hinduism, the soul (atman) moves into new bodies through reincarnation.

Christians and Muslims often believe in Heaven and Hell based on how you lived. Jews focus more on this life but many also believe in an afterlife. Hindus and Buddhists believe in reincarnation, with the ultimate goal of escaping it (moksha or Nirvana).

options: Rebirth of the soul in a new body
Going straight to Heaven
Ending all existence
A type of prayer

mcqs.q: What is the difference between Sunni and Shia Islam?
options: It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
They split over who should lead the Muslim community after Muhammad: Sunnis accepted Abu Bakr and elected caliphs; Shias believed leadership should follow Muhammad's bloodline through Ali.
Sunnis and Shias believe in different gods.
Sunnis follow the Quran and Shias follow the Bible.

mcqs.q: What is the problem of evil?
options: If God is all-loving, all-knowing and all-powerful, why does evil and suffering exist? Logically, all four cannot be true together without explanation.
It is the question of whether evil people will go to hell.
It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
Atman and Brahman are two competing Hindu gods.

mcqs.q: What is the relationship between atman and Brahman in Hindu philosophy?
options: It is the question of whether the devil really exists.

Atman is the individual self/soul; Brahman is ultimate reality. In Advaita Vedanta, atman IS Brahman — the self is identical with ultimate reality, and liberation comes from realising this non-duality.
Atman is the body and Brahman is the soul.
Atman and Brahman are two competing Hindu gods.
